title: SSP-2 — Docs Viewer Project State Delivery
summary: deliver the folder-chaos Project State report and focused Project lookups after typed subject reconciliation
content_html:
SSP-2 — Docs Viewer Project State Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as SSP-2 after SSP-1 projects typed Project subjects through the local Manage manifest. Project State Concept And Architecture owns the model consumed by this delivery.

SSP-2.0 must revise the retained folder-only subject and no-Work-lookup assumptions against the accepted SSP-1 typed subject/association contract before implementation; the existing detailed stages are planning evidence, not authorization to implement the superseded shape.

This delivery builds Project State as a persistent generated Docs Viewer document plus a versioned folder relationship snapshot and Manage-only resolver lookup. It does not retire the existing image-audit workflow; that belongs to SSP-7 — Project Media Audit Delivery.

Complete Outcome

One stable document in scope dotlineform contains the last successfully generated Project State Markdown. Its primary table has exactly three relationship columns: Doc, Folder, and Series. Each normalized folder row may contain several exact Project-document links and several Series links; Works are derivation evidence and are not displayed results.

Running or explicitly refreshing Project State computes the folder-centred snapshot, saved report source, and resolver lookup from one generation, then rebuilds the exact report document. Opening the saved document does not scan the filesystem. Known Docs Viewer and Studio mutations update only affected relationships after their canonical commits; full refresh remains available for direct Finder changes and recovery.

SSP-3 can consume the accepted lookup as soon as its generation, failure, and access contracts are proven. The current /studio/project-state/ route and var/studio/reports/project-state.md remain until SSP-7 preserves and renames their image-audit capability.

Fixed Design Notes

  • The normalized relationship is documents[] <- folder_path -> series[].
  • One row represents one base-relative folder path. Multiple Project documents and multiple Series remain ordered arrays rather than duplicate rows or scalar shortcuts.
  • Works contribute folder evidence and the union of their series_ids; individual Work identities, titles, and URLs are absent from the report and initial resolver lookup.
  • Folder identity is relative to $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/. Initial discovery is rooted at projects/, while exact declared contained targets elsewhere still receive existence and relationship state.
  • The saved report is generated Markdown with a stable doc_id, not a dynamic report module. Manual edits to its generated body are not preserved.
  • Opening displays the last complete report. Explicit Run/Refresh performs the full scan; no filesystem watcher is introduced.
  • The folder lookup returns Series[] + Project documents[] for one exact folder subject. Series items carry semantic catalogue identity rather than stored titles or URLs.
  • Trusted application mutations default to targeted follow-through. Work create/delete, folder fields, and series_ids can change relationships; Work title and project_filename do not.
  • The exact Work observer is server-side after canonical commit and read-only with respect to Studio. It uses exact before/after records, never rewrites Studio, and never makes the canonical commit depend on Project State.
  • Derived-generation failure never rolls back or repeats a committed Work or document mutation. The prior complete generation remains readable and is marked stale.
  • Project State is Manage-only derived data and unusable as canonical truth.

Delivery Discipline

SSP-2 is inherently larger than the completed Projects glue deliveries, so its size must be controlled per checkpoint rather than hidden in one replacement diff. It should compose existing canonical readers, the Projects Manage manifest, exact Docs Viewer source/build seams, generated-payload writers, and server-side post-commit boundaries around one Project-specific producer.

SSP-2.0 must record the exact proposed files and rough production/test diff for the producer/lookup, saved report workflow, and targeted hooks separately. A dynamic report framework, generic graph, event bus, repair system, rewritten catalogue reader, or media-audit migration is scope creep. Each stage stops at its review checkpoint if observed size or dependencies materially exceed the estimate.

Rough Delivery Steps

SSP-2.0 — Trace And Freeze The Replacement

  • [ ] Trace the current folder inventory, canonical Works/Series readers, Projects Manage manifest, generated-document source/build seams, exact mutation follow-through points, and existing generated-payload writers.
  • [ ] Freeze normalized folder identity, input schemas, documents[] and series[] rows, unlinked/invalid evidence, exact links, generation metadata, lookup schema, and stale presentation.
  • [ ] Freeze the stable report document identity, source ownership, three-column Markdown shape, Run/Refresh action, and opening-without-scanning behavior.
  • [ ] Freeze configured discovery roots separately from base-root containment, plus full-refresh triggers, targeted delta shapes, staging/commit order, exact-build behavior, and mutation failure response.
  • [ ] Record exact files, reused seams, and separate rough production/test diff estimates for SSP-2.1, SSP-2.2, and SSP-2.3 before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: one fixture explains every report row and exception plus the precise output affected by Work create/delete, folder change, series_ids change, irrelevant Work title/filename change, Project folder_path change, and Project document create/delete.

SSP-2.1 — Build The Folder-Centred Producer And Lookup

  • [ ] Implement the confined folder-only inventory and normalized reconciliation service.
  • [ ] Read Project-document evidence from the customisation-owned Manage manifest and derive each folder's deduplicated ordered series[] union from canonical Work series_ids.
  • [ ] Retain current, declared, catalogue-only, missing, duplicate-document, unlinked-document, malformed, and incomplete-catalogue evidence.
  • [ ] Publish one versioned snapshot and exact folder-keyed lookup whose initial groups are Series[] + Project documents[].
  • [ ] Prove lookup rows contain semantic Series identities without Work results, Work subjects, stored catalogue URLs, or live-scan fallbacks.

SSP-2.2 — Publish The Saved Docs Viewer Report

  • [ ] Create one stable generated Markdown document in scope dotlineform with a clearly owned body and ordinary Docs Viewer reachability.
  • [ ] Render the Doc/Folder/Series table, compact freshness/count context, exact links, multiple values per cell, and explicit empty/exception states.
  • [ ] Add the explicit Run/Refresh workflow that computes and validates one generation, saves the report source, publishes its matching snapshot/lookup, and rebuilds the exact document.
  • [ ] Preserve the previous complete report and lookup on generation failure; opening the document must never trigger a scan.
  • [ ] Verify Source readability, normal word wrapping, search/bookmark behavior, long cells, and narrow-screen table presentation.

SSP-2.3 — Add Targeted Follow-Through And Verify

  • [ ] Add one Project State impact classifier at the shared server-side Work committed-mutation boundary.
  • [ ] Route create, save, delete, bulk save, and import through complete exact before/after deltas or the explicit full-rebuild fallback.
  • [ ] Add equivalent exact Project-document metadata/create/delete follow-through.
  • [ ] Recompute affected folder memberships for Work folder/Series changes and Project-document folder changes; prove Work title and filename changes do nothing.
  • [ ] Regenerate the compact saved Markdown from the updated snapshot without scanning unrelated inputs.
  • [ ] Preserve the last complete generation and report follow-through failure without retrying the canonical mutation.
  • [ ] Run focused model, normalization, Series-union, generated-document, mutation-delta, generation-agreement, stale-state, exact-link, semantic-descriptor, public-isolation, lint, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Manually review real agreement, no-document, no-Series, prospective, stale, duplicate, moved/renamed, unlinked, error, long-cell, and narrow-screen states.

Not In Scope

  • automatic repair or synchronization;
  • mutation controls in the report;
  • image discovery or primary-image auditing, which belongs to SSP-7;
  • continuous folder watching;
  • public Project State data;
  • retirement of /studio/project-state/ or var/studio/reports/project-state.md, which belongs to SSP-7; or
  • Resolver Token parsing and rendering, which belongs to SSP-3.

Completion Evidence

  • Fixture and real-data evidence prove folder-keyed documents[] and series[] plus every unmatched, duplicate, unlinked, and incomplete state.
  • The saved Docs Viewer document persists the latest successful Doc/Folder/Series Markdown and opens without scanning.
  • Full refresh observes direct Finder changes and publishes one matching report/snapshot/lookup generation.
  • Targeted tests show bounded relationship effects for every relevant Work and Project-document mutation class and no effect for Work title/filename changes.
  • SSP-3 can resolve one folder row to semantic Series descriptors and exact Project-document targets without a live scan.
  • Public projections contain no local folder paths, Project State data, lookup path, service URL, or refresh capability.
  • The current Studio image-audit workflow remains unchanged for SSP-7 rather than being partially retired here.
